payload.claim: Criterion 1's witness (test_an_end_review_grades_each_layer_at_its_branch_head_after_package) and criterion 2's witness (test_a_layer_whose_branch_head_cannot_be_resolved_errors_at_no_cost) each have to single-handedly drive an unusually large bundle of distinct scenarios (three bottom-layer shapes, restacked vs. non-restacked predecessor, a stack-base predecessor with a gone branch, a reserve-stopped walk alongside a run join, a one-layer stack with no join, two different "contains none of its candidates" shapes, and a mid-stack unplaceable layer). The spec's fixture notes describe in detail how to build all of this, and state it was measured and passed on a working prototype, and I did not find a concrete member of either bundle that goes undriven. This is worth a human's attention before a cell spends money, since a test this dense is also the easiest place for a subtly incomplete assertion to let a wrong arm through, but it is not a confirmed `witness` gap.
